data.exact_reserve_text: The 2012, 2013 and 2014 years of account have all shown a profit, with syndicate 1200 being the only syndicate showing a loss. The incoming 2011 and 2012 years of account of RITC produced a technical surplus following continuing favourable incurred development at an attritional level in a number of classes as well as favourable developments on certain individual losses.
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reports a net favourable movement on prior years resulting in a release of reserves. The managing agent states that the incoming 2011 and 2012 RITC years produced a technical surplus driven by continuing favourable incurred development at an attritional level across a number of classes plus favourable development on some individual losses. Overall the prior-year movement aggregated to a net positive contribution to the 2014 result (net prior-year profit ~GBP 9.322m), indicating a release of reserves.
raw_causal_phrases: continuing favourable incurred development at an attritional level in a number of classes
favourable developments on certain individual losses
showed stability of our reserves on all syndicates reinsured into syndicate 2008

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Balance Sheet (Liabilities: Claims outstanding) on page 12 (gross GBP 000). Prior-year development amount derived from the Managing Agent's year-of-account profit breakdown on page 3 (sum of 2012 and 2013 year-of-account profits = GBP 9,322k) and therefore represents NET prior-year development (net of reinsurance). No explicit 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' gross figure or gross claims development triangle was found in the provided pages; RITC activity (incoming 2011 and 2012 years) is mentioned in the report and may distort comparative movements. Prior-year development therefore flagged as NET of reinsurance and reported as a release (-9.322m). If the full notes (movement tables or gross triangle) are available elsewhere in the full accounts, they should be used to replace this net estimate with a gross figure.
